content.content:
Nesh-Deeka: "Then you have seen what a cut is. A Hist that falls silent kills no eggs. The Hist at Low-Reed Village was cut at the root, and the eggs at its roots died of the cut. The interior, the villages inland behind the marsh, must hear that difference. The people who can carry it home gather at Helstrom, a great city behind the marsh. They are the tree-minders, who tend each village's Hist, and the Nisswo, wandering priests who read what a Hist says. I want them to hear what a cut tree looks like from someone the Reed can deny. So you go alone, and I send no escort. Do not name the Reed in Helstrom. If it is named, what you saw becomes the Reed's word and I cannot disown it. I do not like using a hand I can disown. I have no other. Take the coast ship at Lilmoth's stop, on the east side of the town. The ship has a door that opens on Helstrom's landing. Go ashore by it. From the landing the way runs inland over roots and through shallows. Two giant wasps keep the far bend of it, short of the gate. Just inside the gate, to the west, is the grove. Ei-Tuja stands there, a Nisswo who reads for anyone. Kaska-Meen is a tree-minder who sits in the city's assembly and keeps the grove's watch, and she hears few strangers. Go and tell them what you saw. Say only that, as a stranger who saw it."
Objective completed: Tell Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth what happened at Low-Reed Village.
Journal entry (Helstrom Behind Its Marsh): Nesh-Deeka told me a Hist that falls silent kills no eggs, but a cut Hist does, and the villages of the interior must learn the difference. The tree-minders and the Nisswo, the wandering priests who read the Hist, meet at Helstrom behind the marsh. She wants them to hear it from someone the Reed can deny, so I go alone and do not name the Reed. I'm to take the coast ship from Lilmoth's stop and go ashore by its door to Helstrom's river landing.
New objective: Board the coast ship at Lilmoth's stop and go ashore by its door to Helstrom's landing.
Topics:
  1. How do I get to Helstrom?

content.content:
Ei-Tuja: "Then it is not a silence at all. It is a thing done to a tree. I will preach that in every village I walk to. The cutters will hear it with everyone else, and I will say it all the same. Hear this as well. When a Hist dies it leaves a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap that holds the tree's memories. The Aldmeri Dominion used one, long ago, to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Whoever gathers a living tree's sap may be after such a thing. I do not say it is so. I say you should keep it in mind."
